1683:
** ἐμαυτοῦ**, ἐμαυτῆς,
reflexive _pronoun_ of first _person_, **of me, of myself**: only _genitive_, _dative_, and _accusative_ _singular_, both _masculine_ and _feminine_: not found in early _Epic dialect_; _Aeolic dialect_ ἔμ᾽ αὔτῳ, ἔμ᾽ αὔτᾳ, {{Refs 7th c.BC+|7th-6th c.BC: Alcaeus Lyricus 72, 7th-6th c.BC: Sappho Lyrica “Papyrus fragments” in E. Diehl, 15.11, compare 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 80.10}}; ἐμαυτόν is uncertain in {{Refs 6th c.BC+|6th c.BC: Xenophanes Poeta Philosophus (“PLG” 2p.116B.) and 6th c.BC: Anacreon Lyricus 64}}; _Ionic dialect_ ἐμεωυτοῦ {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 4.97 (but ἐμωυτοῦ 2nd c.AD: Apollonius Dyscolus Grammaticus “de Pronominibus;” 74.4), ἐμεωυτῷ 5th c.BC: Herodotus Historicus 3.142, ἐμεωυτόν 1st c.AD(?): Heraclitus 101}}; ἐμᾱτοῦ, ἐμᾱτόν, {{Refs 1st c.BC+|“Lyrica Alexandrina Adespota” 4.23, “SIG” 741.12 (1st c.BC): in _plural_ always separated, ἡμῶν αὐτῶν, etc.}}; ἐν ἐμαυτῷ συννοεῖσθαι in or with **oneself**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th c.BC: Euripides Tragicus “Orestes” 634; πρὸς ἐμαυτόν 5th-6th c.BC: Aristophanes Comicus “Ranae” 53, etc.; strengthened, ἴσχυόν τ᾽ αὐτὸς ἐμαυτοῦ [prev. author] “V.” 357, compare “Lys.” 1125}}; but ἐν ἐμαυτοῦ (i.e. οἴκῳ) εἶναι, _metaphorically_, to be **master of oneself**, {{Refs 5th c.BC+|5th-6th c.BC: Plato Philosophus “Charmides” 155d: _nominative_ ἐμαυτός, com. formation in 5th-6th c.BC: Plato Comicus 78.}}
